items.description: List of useful plugins to make WordPress and Gatsby work together. Ordered alphabetically.
items.title: Plugins
WPGraphQL JWT Authentication
items.description: Extends the WPGraphQL plugin to provide authentication using JWT (JSON Web Tokens).

items.title: WPGraphQL Gutenberg
items.description: Exposes Gutenberg blocks to the WPGraphQL API.

items.title: WPGraphQL Cors
items.description: This FREE plugin from @kidunot89 and @byfunkhaus claims to enable authentication with WPGraphQL to “just work” by allowing you to set CORS headers that GraphQL will accept, which means WordPress default auth cookies can be accepted.

items.title: WPGraphQL Meta Query
items.description: Adds Meta_Query support to the WPGraphQL Plugin for postObject query args.

items.title: WPGraphQL Lock
items.description: Enables query locking for WPGraphQL by implementing persisted GraphQL queries.

items.title: WPGraphQL Send Email
items.description: This FREE plugin from @Ash_Hitchcock allows you to send emails via a simple mutation. Includes the abilitty to restrict sending to trusted origins.

items.title: WPGraphQL Meta
items.description: This FREE plugin from @robertorourke exposes meta registered via the WordPress register_meta API to WPGraphQL.

items.title: WPGraphQL Persisted Queries
items.description: This FREE plugin from @qz adds the ability to use Persisted Queries with WPGraphQL.

items.title: Total Counts for WPGraphQL
items.description: This FREE plugin from @builtbycactus exposes total counts to connections in the WPGraphQL Schema.

items.title: WPGraphQL Offset Pagination
items.description: This FREE plugin from @enshrined adds basic offset pagination as opposed to the standard Cursor based pagination that ships with WPGraphQL.
Note: Since the release of gatsby-source-wordpress V4, it is the preferred over gatsby-source-graphql and therefore I will only list tutorials related to that approach.

items.title: Gatsby + Headless WordPress + Netlify Starter
items.description: A Gatsby + WordPress starter for continuous deployment to Netlify.

items.title: Gatsby Starter - WordPress Twenty Twenty
items.description: A port of the WordPress Twenty Twenty theme to Gatsby using the new gatsby-source-wordpress@v4.

items.title: Gatsby + WPGraphQL Blog Example
items.description: Demo showing how to use WPGraphQL as the source for Gatsby Sites.

items.title: Gatsby WordPress Starter Advanced
items.description: An advanced Gatsby + WordPress starter, that is built along a tutorial series and works with ACF flexible content fields to create content blocks/layouts.

items.title: Gatsby Starter Blog
items.description: Blog starter with enough features to be production ready out of the box.

items.title: Starters

items.description: List of gatsby-themes that work with WordPress as a source, which you can use in your Gatsby setup.

items.title: Twenty Nineteen Gatsby Theme
items.description: A port of the Twenty Nineteen WordPress Theme over to Gatsby.

items.title: Gatsby WordPress Publisher Theme
items.description: The Gatsby Publisher Theme allows you to create a headless (or decoupled) WordPress site. This theme will display all of your pages and posts in a static front-end built on React and Gatsby.
